cases.root_cause: Duration-based pharmacy authorization mismatch; the claim exceeded the allowed days-supply policy for the selected drug.
cases.resolution_used: Validated the payer duration rule, confirmed NDC and days-supply mapping, and routed the claim to the pharmacy exception queue for manual review.
recommended_actions: Validate days-supply against the plan policy.
Check whether the NDC/drug authorization rule was correctly applied.
Escalate the case to pharmacy adjudication for exception review.
cases.impact: Medication dispensation was delayed requiring manual review.
cases.Root_Cause: Prescription refill requested exceeds typical 30/90 day maximum limits without designated prior authorization.
cases.Recommended_Fix: Validate duration rules against the patient's plan policy; verify if an override exists.

cases.root_cause: CPT code mismatch causing drastic variation between standard allowed amounts for the procedural family and the billed amount.
cases.resolution_used: Audit of the attached medical records revealed an incorrect upcoded CPT modifier. Code lowered to match documentation.
recommended_actions: Audit procedural codes against standard modifier rules.
Recalculate allowed amount based on correctly downcoded modifiers.
cases.Root_Cause: Drastic variance between Billed Amount and typical Allowed Amount usually indicates procedural upcoding or incorrect modifiers.
cases.Recommended_Fix: Audit CPT procedural codes against submitted medical records and adjust allowed amounts.

cases.root_cause: The Paid Amount equals the Billed Amount exactly, ignoring contractual network discounts (100% payout ratio).
cases.resolution_used: Flagged for post-payment recovery. Network pricing engine failed to apply the contracted hospital facility discount tier.
recommended_actions: Verify facility network status and active contract clauses.
Manually apply the contractual discount rate.
cases.impact: Significant financial leakage due to missed contractual discount application.
cases.Root_Cause: Paid amount equals Billed amount entirely, meaning the pricing engine failed to apply mandatory network discounts.
cases.Recommended_Fix: Verify the facility's active network contract and manually recalculate the discounted allowed amount.

cases.root_cause: Frequency limitation exceeded for preventative cleaning procedures within a 6 month rolling window.
cases.resolution_used: Automated rejection upheld. Patient history confirmed two prior cleanings in the same calendar year.
recommended_actions: Review member claims history for the past 12 months.
Confirm benefit policy frequency limits (e.g., 2 per year).
Issue patient liability explanation of benefits.
cases.impact: Member is liable for the full billed amount.
cases.Root_Cause: The quantity of procedures billed exceeds plan frequency limitations over a rolling time window.
cases.Recommended_Fix: Check historical patient utilization to confirm frequency rules and uphold the rejection if accurate.

cases.root_cause: The Paid Amount drastically exceeds the calculated Allowed Amount, breaking correlation constraints.
cases.resolution_used: Halted payment. Error in rules engine caused payment to be based on billed rather than allowed amount.
recommended_actions: Recalculate Paid Amount to match Allowed Amount minus co-pays.
Perform QA on the active rules engine deployment.
cases.Root_Cause: A critical financial logic error where the Paid Amount was calculated larger than the Allowed Amount.
cases.Recommended_Fix: Immediately suspend payment. Recalculate Paid Amount capping at the Allowed Amount limit.

cases.root_cause: Data entry error regarding quantity dispensed versus days supply; dispensing 900 pills for 30 days implies 30 pills a day.
cases.resolution_used: Contacted pharmacy for verification. Pharmacy confirmed a typo (meant 90 dispensed). Claim adjusted.
recommended_actions: Verify dosage instructions against quantity and days supply.
Reach out to dispensing pharmacy to confirm actual quantity.
Adjust payout based on corrected clinical metrics.
cases.impact: Corrected large financial discrepancy related to data-entry typo.
cases.Root_Cause: The ratio between Quantity Dispensed and Days Supply is clinically impossible or extremely anomalous.
cases.Recommended_Fix: Flag for data entry review. Contact dispensing provider to confirm the correct dispensed quantity.
